title: Code of Conduct
summary: Sets the standards of honesty, respect, and professional behavior expected of every employee and contractor, and explains how to report a concern without retaliation.

title: Equal Employment Opportunity
summary: Prohibits discrimination in hiring, pay, promotion, and termination on the basis of any protected characteristic, and names HR as the place to raise a complaint.

title: Anti-Harassment
summary: Defines harassment, including sexual harassment, gives examples, and explains how complaints are investigated and kept confidential.

title: Paid Time Off
summary: Explains how vacation and personal days accrue each pay period, how much can carry over into the next year, and how to request time away from work.

title: Holidays
summary: Lists the eleven company holidays and explains holiday pay for people who are scheduled to work on one, such as the weekend clinical line.

title: Remote and Hybrid Work
summary: Explains who may work from home, how many days a week, the equipment the company provides, and the rules for working from another state.

title: Family and Medical Leave (FMLA)
summary: Describes up to twelve weeks of job-protected unpaid leave for a serious health condition, a new child, or caring for a family member, and how to apply.

title: Parental Leave
summary: Provides eight weeks of fully paid leave to birth, adoptive, and foster parents in the first year after the child arrives, on top of any disability benefits.

title: Bereavement Leave
summary: Gives up to five paid days off after the death of a close family member and three days for other relatives, with no documentation required.

title: Jury Duty and Witness Leave
summary: Pays regular wages for up to ten days of jury service and explains what to do when a court summons arrives.

title: Military Leave
summary: Protects the jobs of employees called to military service under USERRA and continues health coverage during the first thirty days.

title: Short-Term Disability
summary: Replaces sixty percent of pay for up to twenty-six weeks when an illness or injury keeps an employee from working, after a seven-day waiting period.

title: Workers' Compensation
summary: Explains what to do after an injury at work: report it the same day, get care, and file the claim with HR within twenty-four hours.

title: Overtime and Timekeeping
summary: Explains who is eligible for overtime, how to record hours accurately, and why working off the clock is never allowed.

title: Payroll Schedule and Pay Stubs
summary: Employees are paid every other Friday by direct deposit; explains how to view pay stubs and correct a payroll error.

title: Performance Reviews
summary: Describes the annual review cycle, the mid-year check-in, the five-point rating scale, and how ratings feed into merit increases.

title: Promotions and Internal Transfers
summary: Explains how to apply for an internal job, when to tell your manager, and the minimum time in role before transferring.

title: Hiring and Background Checks
summary: Describes the background, license, and exclusion-list checks completed before an offer is final, including for contractors with system access.

title: Employee Referral Bonus
summary: Pays a referral bonus when someone you refer is hired and stays ninety days; lists the roles that qualify for a higher bonus.

title: Tuition Assistance
summary: Reimburses up to a yearly limit for job-related courses and degrees, with a pay-back requirement if the employee leaves within a year.

title: Professional License Renewal
summary: The company pays renewal fees and continuing education costs for nursing, pharmacy, and coding credentials required for the job.

title: Dress Code
summary: Business casual in offices, scrubs or business casual for clinical staff on site, and badges visible at all times.

title: Drug-Free Workplace
summary: Prohibits working under the influence and explains when testing happens, such as after a workplace accident.

title: Workplace Violence Prevention
summary: Prohibits threats and weapons on company property and explains how to report a threat or an unsafe situation.

title: Employee Assistance Program
summary: Offers free, confidential counseling sessions and referrals for stress, family, financial, and legal concerns to employees and their households.

title: Health and Dental Benefits for Employees
summary: Summarizes the medical, dental, and vision plans available to employees, open enrollment, and when coverage starts for new hires.

title: Retirement Plan (401(k))
summary: Explains the company match, vesting schedule, automatic enrollment, and how to change contributions.

title: Resignation and Exit Process
summary: Asks for two weeks' notice, explains the final paycheck and PTO payout, and lists the equipment and badges to return on the last day.

title: Progressive Discipline
summary: Describes the steps from verbal warning to termination and the conduct that can skip steps, such as a privacy violation.

title: Personnel Files and Employee Records
summary: Explains what HR keeps in a personnel file, how long it is kept, and how employees can ask to see their own.

title: Flexible Work Schedules
summary: Allows compressed weeks and shifted hours with manager approval, as long as core hours from ten to three are covered.

title: Lactation Accommodation
summary: Provides private lactation rooms and paid break time for nursing parents, at every office.

title: Reasonable Accommodation
summary: Explains how to request a workplace accommodation for a disability or religious practice and how requests are kept confidential.

title: Sepsis Screening and Escalation
summary: Gives the care management nurse line the screening questions for possible sepsis and the steps to escalate to emergency care immediately.

title: Nurse Advice Line Protocols
summary: Lists the symptom-based protocols nurses follow on member calls, when to direct a member to urgent care or the emergency room, and how to document the call.

title: Medication Reconciliation
summary: Describes how care managers compare a member's medication list across prescribers after a hospital discharge and flag interactions to the pharmacist.

title: Care Management Enrollment
summary: Explains which members are offered care management, such as those with heart failure or diabetes, and how outreach and consent work.

title: Transitions of Care After Discharge
summary: Requires a follow-up call within two business days of a hospital discharge to check medications, appointments, and home support.

title: Clinical Documentation Standards
summary: Sets the rules for clinical notes: timely, factual, signed, and never copied forward without review.

title: Medical Necessity Criteria
summary: Explains which nationally recognized criteria clinical reviewers use to decide whether a requested service is medically necessary.

title: Peer-to-Peer Review
summary: Lets an ordering physician discuss a denial with a plan medical director before or after a decision, and sets the scheduling time frames.

title: Utilization Review Time Frames
summary: Sets decision deadlines for standard and expedited prior authorization requests and for concurrent review of inpatient stays.

title: Behavioral Health Crisis Response
summary: Gives nurses the steps to follow when a member expresses thoughts of self-harm, including a warm transfer to the crisis line.

title: Maternity Care Management
summary: Describes outreach to pregnant members, high-risk pregnancy screening, and postpartum follow-up visits.

title: Chronic Kidney Disease Program
summary: Explains how members with advanced kidney disease are identified and connected to nephrology and dialysis planning.

title: Diabetes Management Program
summary: Covers glucose monitoring supplies, education sessions, and the A1c targets care managers track with members.

title: Heart Failure Program
summary: Describes daily weight monitoring, symptom check calls, and when to escalate a member with worsening heart failure.

title: Infection Control in Clinics
summary: Sets hand hygiene, cleaning, and personal protective equipment rules for the on-site employee clinics.

title: Clinical Staff Licensure Verification
summary: Requires primary-source verification of every nurse's and pharmacist's license at hire and before each expiration.

title: Interpreter Services
summary: Explains how to get a qualified medical interpreter for a member call in any language, at no cost to the member.

title: Advance Directives
summary: Explains how care managers talk with members about advance directives and where members can get the forms.

title: Home Health Coordination
summary: Describes how care managers arrange skilled nursing and therapy visits at home after a hospital stay.

title: Durable Medical Equipment Review
summary: Lists the clinical documentation needed to approve wheelchairs, hospital beds, oxygen, and CPAP machines.

title: Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee
summary: Describes how the committee reviews drugs for the formulary, how often it meets, and how conflicts of interest are handled.

title: Opioid Prescribing Safety
summary: Explains the limits on first-fill opioid prescriptions, the morphine-equivalent dose threshold that triggers review, and naloxone outreach.

title: Specialty Pharmacy Management
summary: Covers high-cost specialty drugs, the network specialty pharmacy, and the clinical review required before the first fill.

title: Clinical Quality Measures (HEDIS)
summary: Describes how the plan measures preventive care and chronic condition quality, and how care gaps are sent to providers.

title: Member Health Risk Assessment
summary: Explains the annual health questionnaire, who receives it, and how answers route members into programs.

title: Telehealth Clinical Standards
summary: Sets the rules for video and phone visits through the plan's virtual care vendor, including when an in-person visit is required.

title: Emergency Room Follow-Up
summary: Requires outreach to members after an emergency room visit for a condition that could have been treated in primary care.

title: Preventive Care Reminders
summary: Describes reminder letters and calls for screenings such as mammograms, colonoscopies, and childhood immunizations.

title: Palliative Care Program
summary: Offers symptom management and care planning support to members with serious illness, alongside curative treatment.

title: Case Rounds and Clinical Escalation
summary: Describes the weekly case rounds where complex members are discussed with a medical director and pharmacist.

title: Clinical Incident Reporting
summary: Explains how to report an event that harmed or could have harmed a member, and how incidents are reviewed without blame.

title: Nurse Reviewer Training
summary: Lists the onboarding and annual training required before a nurse makes prior authorization recommendations.

title: Prior Authorization Overview
summary: Explains which services need approval before they are provided, who submits the request, and what happens when a request arrives without one.

title: Prior Authorization Intake
summary: Describes how faxed, portal, and phone requests are logged, checked for missing information, and routed to a nurse reviewer.

title: Urgent and Expedited Requests
summary: Explains when a request qualifies as expedited and the seventy-two-hour decision deadline that applies to it.

title: Retroactive Authorization
summary: Describes the narrow cases, such as emergencies and newborns, in which approval can be requested after the service was provided.

title: Claims Submission Requirements
summary: Lists the information a clean claim must include and the timely filing limit for in-network providers.

title: Claim Denials and Remark Codes
summary: Explains the most common denial reasons, the remark codes on the remittance, and what a provider can fix and resubmit.

title: Member Appeals
summary: Explains how a member appeals a denial, the sixty-day filing window, the review by a clinician not involved in the original decision, and the time frames.

title: Provider Disputes and Reconsiderations
summary: Describes how a provider disputes a payment amount and the difference between a reconsideration and an appeal.

title: External Review
summary: Explains a member's right to an independent external review after the internal appeal is exhausted.

title: Coordination of Benefits
summary: Explains how the plan decides which coverage pays first when a member has more than one plan, including Medicare.

title: Subrogation
summary: Describes how the plan recovers claim costs when another party, such as an auto insurer, is responsible for an injury.

title: Out-of-Network Claims
summary: Explains how out-of-network services are paid, balance billing protections, and when an exception makes them in-network.

title: No Surprises Act Compliance
summary: Describes the protections against surprise bills for emergency care and for out-of-network clinicians at in-network facilities.

title: Claims Payment Accuracy Audits
summary: Describes the monthly sample of paid claims audited for coding and payment errors, and how errors are corrected.

title: Duplicate Claim Detection
summary: Explains how duplicate and overlapping claims are flagged before payment.

title: Fraud, Waste, and Abuse Referrals
summary: Explains the warning signs of billing fraud and how claims staff refer a suspicious pattern to the Special Investigations Unit.

title: Overpayment Recovery
summary: Describes how the plan notifies a provider of an overpayment and the timeline to repay or dispute it.

title: Continuity of Care for New Members
summary: Allows new members in active treatment to keep seeing an out-of-network provider for up to ninety days.

title: Formulary Exception Requests
summary: Explains how a prescriber requests coverage of a drug that is not on the formulary, and the clinical information required.

title: Step Therapy
summary: Explains which drugs require trying a preferred drug first and how to request an exception when it is not appropriate.

title: Member Cost Sharing
summary: Explains deductibles, copays, coinsurance, and the out-of-pocket maximum, with worked examples.

title: Explanation of Benefits Statements
summary: Describes what appears on the EOB a member receives after a claim and how to read it.

title: HIPAA Privacy Rule Overview
summary: Summarizes what protected health information is, the minimum necessary standard, and when PHI may be used or disclosed without authorization.

title: Minimum Necessary Standard
summary: Requires staff to use, request, and disclose only the PHI needed for a task, and gives examples for claims and care management.

title: Member Rights to Access Records
summary: Explains how a member requests a copy of their records, the thirty-day deadline, and the allowed fees.

title: Privacy Incident Reporting
summary: Requires every suspected privacy incident, such as a misdirected fax or email, to be reported to the Privacy Office within one business day.

title: Breach Notification
summary: Describes the risk assessment that decides whether an incident is a reportable breach and the notification deadlines for members and regulators.

title: Business Associate Agreements
summary: Requires a signed BAA before any vendor creates, receives, stores, or transmits PHI for the plan, and names who may sign one.

title: Security Awareness Training
summary: Requires annual privacy and security training for every workforce member, with completion tracked by Compliance.

title: Sanctions for Privacy Violations
summary: Describes the disciplinary consequences of privacy violations, from retraining to termination, based on intent and harm.

title: Records Retention Schedule
summary: Lists how long each type of record is kept, such as claims for ten years, and how records are destroyed at the end.

title: Secure Disposal of PHI
summary: Requires shredding of paper PHI in locked bins and certified destruction of drives and devices.

title: Fax Handling Procedure
summary: Requires confirming fax numbers, using the cover sheet, sending only necessary pages, and reporting misdirected faxes.

title: Email and Messaging with PHI
summary: Requires encryption for external email containing PHI and prohibits PHI in text messages and chat tools that are not approved.

title: De-identification of Data
summary: Explains the Safe Harbor and Expert Determination methods and who must approve a de-identified data set before it is shared.

title: Research Use of Member Data
summary: Requires Privacy Board approval before member data is used for research, and explains limited data sets and data use agreements.

title: Marketing and Member Communications
summary: Explains when marketing to members requires their authorization and which communications are exempt.

title: Conflicts of Interest
summary: Requires annual disclosure of outside interests and gifts that could influence business decisions.

title: Gifts and Entertainment
summary: Limits gifts from vendors and providers to a small value and prohibits cash or gift cards.

title: Compliance Hotline
summary: Describes the anonymous hotline for reporting fraud, privacy, and ethics concerns, and the no-retaliation guarantee.

title: Exclusion List Screening
summary: Requires monthly screening of employees, contractors, and providers against federal and state exclusion lists.

title: Regulatory Audits and Inquiries
summary: Explains how to respond to a regulator's request: route it to Compliance the same day and do not send documents directly.

title: Accounting of Disclosures
summary: Explains a member's right to a list of certain disclosures of their PHI and how Compliance tracks them.

title: Mental Health Parity Compliance
summary: Describes how the plan checks that limits on mental health and substance use benefits are no stricter than medical ones.

title: Language Access and Nondiscrimination
summary: Describes the notice of nondiscrimination, taglines in other languages, and free interpreter and translation services.

title: Policy Management
summary: Explains how policies are written, approved, numbered, reviewed every year, and retired.

title: Acceptable Use of Systems
summary: Sets the rules for using company laptops, email, and internet, including what personal use is allowed and what is monitored.

title: Password and Passphrase Standard
summary: Requires passphrases of at least fourteen characters and multi-factor sign-in, and explains how to reset a forgotten password.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication
summary: Requires multi-factor sign-in for every account, and explains how to set up the authenticator app and what to do with a lost phone.

title: Remote Access and VPN
summary: Explains how to connect to internal systems from home, why public Wi-Fi requires the VPN, and which systems are reachable remotely.

title: Bring Your Own Device
summary: Allows company email on personal phones only with the device management app installed and a screen lock enabled.

title: Laptop Encryption and Lost Devices
summary: Requires full-disk encryption on every laptop and immediate reporting of a lost or stolen device to the service desk.

title: Access Requests and Approvals
summary: Explains how to request access to an application, who approves it, and how access is removed when a role changes.

title: Quarterly Access Reviews
summary: Requires managers to review and confirm their team's application access every quarter.

title: Phishing Reporting
summary: Explains how to recognize a phishing email and report it with the button in Outlook, and what happens next.

title: Software Installation
summary: Allows only approved software from the company portal and explains how to request something new.

title: Generative AI Use
summary: Allows only approved AI tools, prohibits entering PHI or confidential data into consumer chatbots, and names PriorAuthBot as the approved internal assistant.

title: Data Classification
summary: Defines the four classification levels, Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted, with examples of each.

title: Backup and Recovery
summary: Describes how often systems are backed up, how long backups are kept, and how restores are tested.

title: Change Management
summary: Requires a reviewed and approved change ticket for production changes, with an emergency process for outages.

title: Incident Response
summary: Describes how security incidents are detected, triaged, contained, and reported, and who is on the response team.

title: Vendor Security Reviews
summary: Requires a security review before buying any software or service that will store company or member data.

title: Logging and Monitoring
summary: Describes which systems send logs to the security monitoring platform and how long logs are kept.

title: Vulnerability Management
summary: Sets patching deadlines by severity, such as fourteen days for critical vulnerabilities.

title: Service Desk Support
summary: Explains how to open a ticket, the support hours, and response targets by priority.

title: Printing and Scanning
summary: Requires secure release printing for documents with PHI and explains scan-to-email limits.

title: Collaboration Tools
summary: Lists the approved chat, meeting, and file-sharing tools and the rules for sharing files with outside parties.

title: Shared Mailboxes
summary: Explains how to request a shared mailbox and who owns access to it.

title: Developer Secure Coding Standard
summary: Requires code review, dependency scanning, and secrets in a vault rather than in source code.

title: Cloud Usage
summary: Requires all cloud resources to be created in company subscriptions with tagging, and prohibits personal cloud accounts for work data.

title: Business Travel
summary: Explains how to book travel through the company travel tool, the hotel and meal limits, and how to submit expenses within thirty days.

title: Expense Reimbursement
summary: Lists what can be expensed, the receipts required, and how quickly reimbursements are paid.

title: Corporate Credit Cards
summary: Explains who receives a corporate card, what it can be used for, and the monthly reconciliation deadline.

title: Office Access and Badges
summary: Requires badges to be worn and never shared, and explains how visitors are signed in and escorted.

title: Visitors in the Office
summary: Visitors sign in at reception, wear a visitor badge, and stay with their host, and may not enter areas where PHI is handled.

title: Emergency Evacuation
summary: Describes fire alarms, evacuation routes, and assembly points for each office.

title: Inclement Weather
summary: Explains how office closures are announced and when employees should work from home.

title: Social Media
summary: Explains what employees may and may not post about the company, members, and coworkers.

title: Media Inquiries
summary: Requires that all questions from reporters be sent to Communications without comment.

title: Charitable Giving and Volunteering
summary: Provides one paid volunteer day per year and a donation match up to a yearly limit.

title: Company Vehicles
summary: Lists who may drive a company vehicle, the insurance requirements, and how to report an accident.

title: Mail and Shipping
summary: Explains how to send overnight packages and certified mail, and how incoming mail with PHI is handled.

title: Purchasing and Approval Limits
summary: Lists who may approve purchases at each amount and when a purchase order is required.

title: Records Requests from Employees
summary: Explains how employees request employment verification letters and copies of tax forms.

title: Recycling and Sustainability
summary: Describes office recycling and the program to reduce printing.

title: Parking and Commuting
summary: Explains parking permits at each office and the pre-tax transit benefit.

title: Food in the Office
summary: Explains kitchen rules and the policy on catered meetings.

title: Employee Directory
summary: Explains how to update your title, phone, and photo in the directory.

title: Holiday Gifts to Members and Providers
summary: Prohibits gifts to members and limits gifts to providers to items of nominal value.

title: Company Events
summary: Covers conduct, alcohol, and expense rules for company-sponsored events.

title: Coverage criteria: MRI of the lumbar spine
summary: Prior authorization is required for MRI of the lumbar spine (CPT 72148). It is approved after six weeks of documented conservative treatment, unless red-flag symptoms are present.

title: Coverage criteria: MRI of the brain
summary: Prior authorization is required for MRI of the brain (CPT 70553). It is approved for new neurological deficits, suspected tumor, or seizures not explained by prior imaging.

title: Coverage criteria: CT of the abdomen and pelvis
summary: Prior authorization is required for CT of the abdomen and pelvis (CPT 74177). It is approved when ultrasound is not diagnostic or not appropriate for the suspected condition.

title: Coverage criteria: PET scan for cancer staging
summary: Prior authorization is required for PET scan for cancer staging (CPT 78815). It is approved for initial staging and restaging of cancers where it changes management.

title: Coverage criteria: Knee arthroscopy
summary: Prior authorization is required for knee arthroscopy (CPT 29881). It is approved for mechanical symptoms with imaging-confirmed meniscal tear after failed physical therapy.

title: Coverage criteria: Total knee replacement
summary: Prior authorization is required for total knee replacement (CPT 27447). It is approved for advanced arthritis with functional limitation after conservative treatment.

title: Coverage criteria: Total hip replacement
summary: Prior authorization is required for total hip replacement (CPT 27130). It is approved for advanced arthritis or avascular necrosis with documented functional limitation.

title: Coverage criteria: Lumbar spinal fusion
summary: Prior authorization is required for lumbar spinal fusion (CPT 22612). It is approved for instability or deformity with neurological findings, after a shared decision-making visit.

title: Coverage criteria: Bariatric surgery (sleeve gastrectomy)
summary: Prior authorization is required for bariatric surgery (sleeve gastrectomy) (CPT 43775). It is approved for adults meeting body mass index criteria who completed a supervised weight management program.

title: Coverage criteria: Sleep study in a lab
summary: Prior authorization is required for sleep study in a lab (CPT 95810). It is approved when a home sleep test is not appropriate or was inconclusive.

title: Coverage criteria: Home sleep apnea test
summary: Prior authorization is required for home sleep apnea test (CPT 95806). It is approved for adults with suspected moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea.

title: Coverage criteria: CPAP device
summary: Prior authorization is required for CPAP device (HCPCS E0601). It is approved after a sleep study confirms obstructive sleep apnea; continued coverage requires adherence data.

title: Coverage criteria: Outpatient physical therapy beyond 20 visits
summary: Prior authorization is required for outpatient physical therapy beyond 20 visits (CPT 97110). It is approved with documented functional progress toward measurable goals.

title: Coverage criteria: Speech therapy
summary: Prior authorization is required for speech therapy (CPT 92507). It is approved for speech or swallowing disorders with a treatment plan and measurable goals.

title: Coverage criteria: Genetic testing for hereditary cancer (BRCA1/BRCA2)
summary: Prior authorization is required for genetic testing for hereditary cancer (brca1/brca2) (CPT 81162). It is approved when personal or family history meets national testing criteria and results will change care.

title: Coverage criteria: Upper endoscopy
summary: Prior authorization is required for upper endoscopy (CPT 43239). It is approved for persistent symptoms, alarm features, or surveillance of known conditions.

title: Coverage criteria: Colonoscopy (diagnostic)
summary: Prior authorization is required for colonoscopy (diagnostic) (CPT 45378). It is approved for symptoms or abnormal screening results; screening colonoscopy needs no authorization.

title: Coverage criteria: Cardiac catheterization
summary: Prior authorization is required for cardiac catheterization (CPT 93458). It is approved for suspected coronary disease with positive or inconclusive noninvasive testing.

title: Coverage criteria: Echocardiogram (transthoracic)
summary: Prior authorization is required for echocardiogram (transthoracic) (CPT 93306). It is approved for new symptoms, murmurs, or changes in known heart disease.

title: Coverage criteria: Cardiac stress test with imaging
summary: Prior authorization is required for cardiac stress test with imaging (CPT 78452). It is approved when a standard exercise test is not possible or not diagnostic.

title: Coverage criteria: Spinal cord stimulator trial
summary: Prior authorization is required for spinal cord stimulator trial (CPT 63650). It is approved for chronic pain after failed conservative and surgical treatment, with a psychological evaluation.

title: Coverage criteria: Epidural steroid injection
summary: Prior authorization is required for epidural steroid injection (CPT 62323). It is approved for radicular pain with imaging correlation, limited to a set number per year.

title: Coverage criteria: Radiofrequency ablation of spinal nerves
summary: Prior authorization is required for radiofrequency ablation of spinal nerves (CPT 64635). It is approved after two positive diagnostic medial branch blocks.

title: Coverage criteria: Cataract surgery
summary: Prior authorization is required for cataract surgery (CPT 66984). It is approved when vision loss limits daily activities and cannot be corrected with glasses.

title: Coverage criteria: Hysterectomy (laparoscopic)
summary: Prior authorization is required for hysterectomy (laparoscopic) (CPT 58571). It is approved after documented failure or contraindication of less invasive treatment.

title: Coverage criteria: Septoplasty
summary: Prior authorization is required for septoplasty (CPT 30520). It is approved for nasal obstruction with documented failure of medical therapy.

title: Coverage criteria: Tonsillectomy for adults
summary: Prior authorization is required for tonsillectomy for adults (CPT 42826). It is approved for recurrent tonsillitis meeting frequency criteria or for obstructive symptoms.

title: Coverage criteria: Varicose vein ablation
summary: Prior authorization is required for varicose vein ablation (CPT 36475). It is approved for symptomatic venous reflux after a trial of compression stockings.

title: Coverage criteria: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
summary: Prior authorization is required for hyperbaric oxygen therapy (CPT 99183). It is approved for specific approved indications such as non-healing diabetic foot ulcers.

title: Coverage criteria: Inpatient rehabilitation admission
summary: Prior authorization is required for inpatient rehabilitation admission. It is approved when the member needs and can tolerate intensive therapy three hours a day.

title: Coverage criteria: Skilled nursing facility admission
summary: Prior authorization is required for skilled nursing facility admission. It is approved after a qualifying need for daily skilled care that cannot be provided at home.

title: Coverage criteria: Home infusion therapy
summary: Prior authorization is required for home infusion therapy (CPT 99601). It is approved for intravenous drugs that can be safely given at home with nursing support.

title: Coverage criteria: Proton beam therapy
summary: Prior authorization is required for proton beam therapy (CPT 77520). It is approved for tumors near critical structures where the dose benefit over standard radiation is documented.

title: Coverage criteria: Insulin pump
summary: Prior authorization is required for insulin pump (HCPCS E0784). It is approved for members with diabetes on multiple daily injections who meet monitoring criteria.

title: Coverage criteria: Continuous glucose monitor
summary: Prior authorization is required for continuous glucose monitor (HCPCS A9276). It is approved for members on insulin or with documented problematic hypoglycemia.

title: Coverage criteria: Power wheelchair
summary: Prior authorization is required for power wheelchair (HCPCS K0823). It is approved when a manual wheelchair or scooter cannot meet the member's mobility needs at home.

title: Coverage criteria: Applied behavior analysis for autism
summary: Prior authorization is required for applied behavior analysis for autism (CPT 97153). It is approved with a diagnosis, a treatment plan, and progress reviews every six months.

title: Coverage criteria: Transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression
summary: Prior authorization is required for transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression (CPT 90867). It is approved after at least two failed antidepressant trials and psychotherapy.

title: Coverage criteria: Residential substance use treatment
summary: Prior authorization is required for residential substance use treatment (HCPCS H0018). It is approved when withdrawal risk or relapse history makes outpatient care unsafe.

title: Coverage criteria: Gender-affirming surgery
summary: Prior authorization is required for gender-affirming surgery. It is approved with documentation from treating clinicians that national criteria are met.
